newsitem.title: UK: UK watchdog delays widening of gas competition.
newsitem.headline: UK watchdog delays widening of gas competition.

text.p: Industry regulator Ofgas on Tuesday delayed the extension of competition in the British household gas market, after a pilot project in the south west of England was plagued by billing problems for British Gas.

The four-week delay means that competition will be introduced in Avon and Dorset in February instead of January, while households in Sussex and Kent, in the south of England, will have to wait until March before they can choose between different gas suppliers.
"The reason we've done is this is to allow British Gas to prepare their computer system," said an Ofgas spokesman.

British Gas faced a surge in complaints after it introduced a single computerised billing system for all its customers in April. Hundreds of customers were sent wrong bills or reminder letters for bills they did not owe.

The company apologised, saying the faults were caused by teething problems following the rapid introduction of competition in the domestic market, which had left it insufficient time to test the billing system.
But British Gas on Tuesday refused to guarantee the system would be working satisfactory after the announced delay.
"We remain concerned that by introducing phase two of competition during the winter period there may ultimately be difficulties for customers switching suppliers," the utility said in a statement.
The Gas Consumers Council welcomed the delay of competition in Avon, Dorset, Sussex and Kent, saying the process now stood a better chance of success.
"Too many consumers experienced inaccurate final meter reads and received disputed final bills," said Sue Slipam, director of the council.
"If these problems are not ironed out by the start of Phase Two it could bring domestic competition in disrepute," she added.
